Daily Digest · Computer Science

Agents Learn to Act in Real Worlds

Today's papers chart a decisive shift: from agents that merely understand to agents that manipulate, navigate, and control physical reality. Whether through robotics benchmarks, world models predicting particle motion, or AI-scientists running live research environments, the frontier has moved from perception to agency. The surprise isn't capability—it's that we're now measuring success by what agents can *do* rather than what they can describe.

⚡ Highlighted Findings 4 selected · AI-curated
Robotics
World Models That Predict Real Physics in 3D

GPWM generates 3D particle motion directly in physical space rather than predicting video appearance, covering rigid bodies, cloth, and granular materials. This single representation handles both passive physics and robotic interaction, a major departure from vision-centric approaches.

A single architecture generalizes across fundamentally different material types—rigid, deformable, cloth, and granular—with coherent predictions far beyond training horizon.
Ren, Bronars et al. 2611.08338 PDF
Machine Learning
Foundation Model for Raw Inertial Sensor Data

IMUDINO is the first foundation model for inertial sensing (accelerometers, gyroscopes) achieving competitive performance across human activity recognition, health monitoring, motion capture, and odometry. It handles variable input lengths and sensor locations—major practical constraints prior models ignored.

A single FM outperforms task-specific supervised baselines in human activity recognition, traditionally dominated by specialized methods.
Ye, Zhang et al. 2611.07437 PDF
Computer Vision
Topology Meets Vision Transformers for Medical Images

TRiST embeds persistent homology (topological structure) directly into hierarchical vision transformer layers, not as post-processing. Medical images encode topological patterns—connected components, loops—that CNNs and standard transformers ignore entirely.

Integrating 2D persistent homology into multi-scale attention improves detection of lesions and organ boundaries by explicitly modeling topological invariants.
Gu, Li et al. 2611.07431 PDF
AI Safety
Multimodal Social Engineering Attacks on AI Agents

Multimodal-SEA benchmarks 608 real-world social engineering tasks spanning 14 domains with forged images, videos, and text—the first comprehensive evaluation of agent security under coordinated multimodal attacks. Current agents are evaluated almost exclusively on text-based dialogue.

Personal AI agents show significant vulnerability to multimodal fraud scenarios combining deepfakes, fake documents, and social context—a security gap not captured by existing benchmarks.
He, Zhang et al. 2611.08281 PDF

RM-VLM: From Natural-Language Task Descriptions to Vision-Grounded Reward Machines

Proposes RM-VLM to automatically ground natural language task descriptions into vision-based reward machines, eliminating manual labeling functions. Uses vision-language models to extract propositions directly from observations, enabling reward machines to work in new environments without per-environment engineering.

02
CardioLM: A Multilingual Suite for Cardiology Domain

Presents CardioCCC, a multilingual cardiology corpus of 508 case reports across 7 languages with clinical entity annotations. Develops CardioLM, small language models fine-tuned for cardiology NLP tasks, addressing the gap where clinical NLP resources concentrate in English.

03
Agent-Native Primitives for Real-World Task Solving

Identifies the 'last mile' failure mode where agents reach a resource but fail to apply it (37–52% task failure rate on Terminal-Bench). Introduces agent-native primitives—reusable components that equip resources with application competence, enabling end-to-end real-world task execution.

cs.CLcs.AIJin, Kuang, YuanPDF
04
Hierarchical Mixture-of-Experts for 3D Medical Vision-Language

MedHiVE combines hierarchical Soft Mixture-of-Experts with contrastive learning to model 3D medical scans and radiology reports together. Routes both vision and text tokens through anatomically organized expert layers, capturing the hierarchical structure of diagnostic reasoning.

cs.CVMert, Płotka, BassiPDF
05
La-JEPA: Compact Robot Policies with Latent World Modeling

Introduces Latent Action JEPA, a lightweight world-action model for robot control trained from scratch in the feature space of a pretrained encoder. Decouples policy architecture from generation-oriented design choices, reducing inference cost while maintaining control performance.

cs.ROcs.CVClémente, Xue, AbyanehPDF
06
IMUDINO: Self-distilled Foundation Model for Inertial Sensing

Presents the first foundation model for inertial measurement unit (IMU) data, achieving competitive performance across human activity recognition, health monitoring, motion capture, and odometry. Handles variable input lengths, sampling rates, and sensor locations—constraints prior FM approaches ignore.

cs.LGcs.AIYe, Zhang, WangPDF
07
TRiST: Topology-Reinforced Swin Transformer for Medical Images

Integrates topological information (persistent homology H0 and H1) into hierarchical vision transformer layers for medical image analysis. Embeds topological structure into feature construction and attention mechanisms, capturing lesion connectivity and organ boundaries.

cs.CVGu, Li, MengPDF
08
Scientist World: Executable Environments for AI-Scientists

Converts 1,000 research papers into executable environments where AI-Scientists can reproduce methods and explore open problems. Each environment extracts the paper's research question and implements the baseline, creating a runnable world for autonomous research agents.

cs.AIcs.CLLu, Konan, LiuPDF
09
XStack: ML Repository Migration Benchmark

Introduces XStack, a benchmark for evaluating agents on migrating ML code between PyTorch/NVIDIA and JAX/TPU ecosystems. Tests long-horizon reasoning across frameworks and hardware, covering full repositories rather than isolated code snippets.

cs.LGcs.AICai, Lu, ChenPDF
10
On the Limitations of Molecular Representations

Systematically evaluates molecular embeddings (fingerprints, learned representations) and finds that state-of-the-art models fail to capture graph structure, 3D shape, or ADMET properties. Reveals gaps between downstream task performance and true representation quality.

cs.LGBlake, Imrie, DeanePDF
11
GPWM: Generative Particle World Model for Physical Scenes

Introduces GPWM, predicting 3D scene evolution through particle and rigid body motion rather than video appearance. Single architecture handles rigid, deformable, cloth, and granular materials with coherent long-horizon predictions using flow matching and diffusion forcing.

cs.RORen, Bronars, ZhuPDF
12
Multimodal-SEA: Security Under Social Engineering Attacks

Benchmark of 608 expert-designed tasks testing AI agents against multimodal social engineering attacks with forged images, videos, and text across 14 domains. Reveals security gaps in personal AI agents evaluated only on text-based dialogue.

cs.CLHe, Zhang, HanPDF
13
SSoG: Separable Gaussian Operators for Vision Transformers

Replaces quadratic self-attention with learned mixtures of axis-factorized Gaussian kernels, reducing per-layer cost from O(N²) to subquadratic. Maintains global Lipschitz continuity via fixed kernels, guaranteeing stable ODE-based vision transformer dynamics.

14
RoboARCade: Benchmarking Agentic Robot Control

Benchmark of long-horizon manipulation tasks across three robot embodiments testing agentic control (agents as direct policies). Tasks emphasize in-context adaptation, memory, and reasoning for precise control with widened initial condition ranges.

15
Describe Facial Expressions by Linking Image Encoders and LLMs

Proposes facial expression captioning—describing facial actions and emotional states in natural language beyond emotion categories or AUs. Uses three-stage training with BLIP-2 and synthesized image-text pairs to overcome training data scarcity.

16
StitchEdit: Stitching Depth Priors into Image Editors

Discovers via per-layer gradient probing that depth objectives conflict with diffusion-based editing in late transformer layers. Proposes technique to redirect geometric priors from pretrained diffusion models toward spatial image editing (object manipulation, viewpoint changes).

17
STAG-Net: Structure-Aware Attention for Head Pose Estimation

Lightweight head pose estimator using facial landmarks with structure-aware attention, spatial clustering, and compact DeepSet encoders. Designed for resource-constrained deployment in driver monitoring and human-computer interaction.

UniGADD: Universal Generator-Agnostic Deepfake Detector

Two-stage method combining contrastive learning (strong performance on known generators) with distribution refinement (robustness to unseen generators). Learns discriminative embeddings that generalize beyond training deepfake sources.

Echoes of Error: Residual-Directional Rollout Consistency

Formalizes rollout error propagation in time-series forecasting through local rollout consistency. Proposes method to enforce consistency by tracking residual-induced perturbations between teacher-forced and free-running predictions.

MessyNav: Zero-Shot Navigation via Manipulation

Formalizes open-world interactive navigation where robots must manipulate obstacles to clear navigation paths. Enables zero-shot generalization across novel objects and environments without per-scene instructions or simulation training.

In-Context Control of Dynamical Systems with Transformers

Investigates whether Transformers can perform 'in-context' control of unstable nonlinear dynamical systems given only system family and unforced dynamics context. Leverages GPT-2-style architecture for low-level closed-loop control.

Edge-Assisted Crowdsensing for Cyclist Safety Perception

Combines handlebar cameras, vision-language models, and explainable boosting machines to predict perceived cycling safety along routes. Integrates street-level vision with OpenStreetMap infrastructure and on-bike kinematics for continuous monitoring.

MedGraph: Graph Memory for Long-Term Medical Dialogue

Graph-based memory system for LLM medical assistants following patients across visits. Addresses three recurring errors: outdated health facts, mixed patient records, and missing safety information through dated fact extraction and person-attribution.

Benchmarks as Software: Continuous Benchmark Validation

Proposes continuous validation framework for benchmarks like Terminal-Bench, addressing 'benchmark maintenance debt' where stale verifiers reject valid model solutions and infrastructure changes invalidate assumptions. Treats benchmarks as living software.

Adaptive Low-Light Enhancement for Road Anomaly Detection

Benchmarks YOLOv8n, YOLOv12n, RT-DETR, and Faster R-CNN under degraded visual conditions. Shows uniform SCI enhancement is harmful at dusk; proposes lightweight luminance-adaptive router selecting no enhancement, moderate, or denoised enhancement.
